+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import duckdb
+import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
+import pandas as pd
+
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).parent
+DATA = ROOT / "data" / "crashes.parquet"
+OUT = ROOT / "out"
+OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
+con = duckdb.connect()
+
+coverage = con.execute(
+    "SELECT count(*) AS n, min(crash_date) AS first_date, max(crash_date) AS last_date, "
+    "count(*) FILTER (WHERE crash_date IS NULL OR crash_time IS NULL) AS missing_time_date "
+    "FROM read_parquet(?)", [str(DATA)]
+).fetchdf().iloc[0]
+start = pd.Timestamp(coverage.first_date)
+end = pd.Timestamp(coverage.last_date)
+days = (end - start).days + 1
+
+base = """
+WITH x AS (
+  SELECT crash_date, crash_time,
+         number_of_persons_injured AS injured,
+         number_of_persons_killed AS killed,
+         CASE WHEN crash_time >= TIME '06:00:00' AND crash_time < TIME '18:00:00'
+              THEN 'Day (6 a.m.–5:59 p.m.)'
+              ELSE 'Night (6 p.m.–5:59 a.m.)' END AS period
+  FROM read_parquet(?)
+)
+"""
+query_params = [str(DATA)]
+counts = con.execute(base + """
+SELECT period, count(*) AS crashes,
+       count(*) FILTER (WHERE injured IS NOT NULL AND killed IS NOT NULL) AS complete_crashes,
+       count(*) FILTER (WHERE injured IS NULL OR killed IS NULL) AS missing_severity,
+       count(*) FILTER (WHERE injured IS NOT NULL AND killed IS NOT NULL
+                        AND (injured > 0 OR killed > 0)) AS casualty_crashes,
+       sum(killed) FILTER (WHERE injured IS NOT NULL AND killed IS NOT NULL) AS deaths
+FROM x GROUP BY period
+""", query_params).set_index("period")
+periods = ["Day (6 a.m.–5:59 p.m.)", "Night (6 p.m.–5:59 a.m.)"]
+counts = counts.reindex(periods)
+
+missing_share = float(counts.missing_severity.sum() / int(coverage.n) * 100)
+missing_n = int(counts.missing_severity.sum())
+total_n = int(coverage.n)
+
+def save_chart(df, id_, title, ylabel, value_col, fmt, footnote):
+    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8.2, 5.1))
+    colors = ["#2878B5", "#E07A2D"]
+    bars = ax.bar(df["period"], df[value_col], color=colors, width=0.58)
+    ax.set_title(title, loc="left", fontsize=15, weight="bold", pad=14)
+    ax.set_ylabel(ylabel)
+    ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
+    ax.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.22)
+    ax.set_axisbelow(True)
+    ax.tick_params(axis="x", labelsize=10)
+    for bar, value in zip(bars, df[value_col]):
+        ax.annotate(fmt(value), (bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2, bar.get_height()),
+                    xytext=(0, 5), textcoords="offset points", ha="center", fontsize=11)
+    fig.text(0.01, 0.015, footnote, fontsize=8.5, color="#555555")
+    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0.07, 1, 1))
+    fig.savefig(OUT / f"option_{id_}.png", dpi=180, bbox_inches="tight")
+    plt.close(fig)
+
+
+# Framing 1: reported crash counts per clock hour in equal 12-hour windows.
+hours = days * 12
+volume = pd.DataFrame({"period": periods})
+volume["crash_count"] = [int(counts.loc[p, "crashes"]) for p in periods]
+volume["observed_hours"] = hours
+volume["crashes_per_hour"] = volume.crash_count / volume.observed_hours
+volume.to_csv(OUT / "values_1.csv", index=False, float_format="%.6f")
+save_chart(volume, 1, "Reported crashes per clock hour", "Crashes per clock hour",
+           "crashes_per_hour", lambda v: f"{v:.1f}",
+           "Equal 12-hour windows; crash records do not measure traffic exposure or per-trip risk.")
+
+# Framing 2: fraction of crashes with any reported injury or death.
+severity = pd.DataFrame({"period": periods})
+severity["crashes_with_injury_or_death"] = [int(counts.loc[p, "casualty_crashes"]) for p in periods]
+severity["crashes_with_complete_injury_and_death_counts"] = [int(counts.loc[p, "complete_crashes"]) for p in periods]
+severity["share_with_injury_or_death_pct"] = (
+    severity.crashes_with_injury_or_death /
+    severity.crashes_with_complete_injury_and_death_counts * 100
+)
+severity["missing_severity_rows"] = [int(counts.loc[p, "missing_severity"]) for p in periods]
+severity.to_csv(OUT / "values_2.csv", index=False, float_format="%.6f")
+save_chart(severity, 2, "Crashes involving injury or death", "Share of crashes with injury or death (%)",
+           "share_with_injury_or_death_pct", lambda v: f"{v:.2f}%",
+           "Denominator includes crashes with both injury and death counts reported; unknown counts are excluded.")
+
+# Framing 3: deaths recorded per crash with complete injury and death counts.
+fatality = pd.DataFrame({"period": periods})
+fatality["deaths"] = [int(counts.loc[p, "deaths"]) for p in periods]
+fatality["crashes_with_complete_injury_and_death_counts"] = [int(counts.loc[p, "complete_crashes"]) for p in periods]
+fatality["deaths_per_crash"] = fatality.deaths / fatality.crashes_with_complete_injury_and_death_counts
+fatality["missing_severity_rows"] = [int(counts.loc[p, "missing_severity"]) for p in periods]
+fatality.to_csv(OUT / "values_3.csv", index=False, float_format="%.8f")
+save_chart(fatality, 3, "Recorded deaths per crash", "Deaths per crash with complete severity counts",
+           "deaths_per_crash", lambda v: f"{v:.4f}",
+           "Each death is counted; crashes missing either injury or death counts are excluded.")
+
+def val(df, col, i):
+    return float(df.iloc[i][col])
+
+def partial_coverage_text():
+    return ("The file covers 2012 only from July 1 (182 of 366 calendar days, 49.7% outside the file) "
+            "and 2026 only through June 11 (203 of 365 days, 55.6% outside the file).")
+
+day, night = 0, 1
+rate1_d, rate1_n = val(volume, "crashes_per_hour", day), val(volume, "crashes_per_hour", night)
+rate2_d, rate2_n = val(severity, "share_with_injury_or_death_pct", day), val(severity, "share_with_injury_or_death_pct", night)
+rate3_d, rate3_n = val(fatality, "deaths_per_crash", day), val(fatality, "deaths_per_crash", night)
+
+options = {"options": [
+    {
+        "id": 1,
+        "metric": "Police-reported crash count per clock hour",
+        "denominator": f"12-hour periods per calendar date across {days} dates ({hours} hours per period)",
+        "grouping": "Day 6 a.m.–5:59 p.m. versus night 6 p.m.–5:59 a.m.",
+        "chart_type": "Two-bar comparison",
+        "reason": "Equal-length day and night windows make the volume comparison straightforward while adjusting for hours in each window.",
+        "probability": 0.32,
+        "answer": f"Police-reported crashes averaged {rate1_n:.1f} per clock hour at night versus {rate1_d:.1f} by day, so the file records fewer crashes per hour at night, not a measure of per-trip danger.",
+        "interpretation": f"This framing answers whether more police-reported crashes occur at night by comparing reported crashes per clock hour in equal 12-hour windows; the chart shows {rate1_n:.1f} at night and {rate1_d:.1f} by day. Equal-duration windows are a defensible way to compare incident volume by time of day, but this file has no traffic or pedestrian exposure denominator and therefore cannot establish that a trip or street user is more at risk at night. No rows are left out for missing date or time ({int(coverage.missing_time_date)} of {total_n}, 0.0%). {partial_coverage_text()}"
+    },
+    {
+        "id": 2,
+        "metric": "Share of crashes with at least one person injured or killed",
+        "denominator": "Crash records with both person-injured and person-killed counts non-NULL",
+        "grouping": "Day 6 a.m.–5:59 p.m. versus night 6 p.m.–5:59 a.m.",
+        "chart_type": "Two-bar comparison",
+        "reason": "A per-crash casualty share compares how often reported crashes involve harm rather than how many crashes occur overall.",
+        "probability": 0.43,
+        "answer": f"Among crashes with complete casualty counts, {rate2_n:.2f}% at night involved an injury or death, compared with {rate2_d:.2f}% by day.",
+        "interpretation": f"This framing answers whether a reported crash is more likely to involve harm at night, defining harm as at least one person injured or killed; the chart shows {rate2_n:.2f}% of complete nighttime records versus {rate2_d:.2f}% of daytime records. The per-crash denominator is defensible for comparing crash severity, though it does not estimate a street user's risk per trip or mile. It leaves out {missing_n} of {total_n} rows ({missing_share:.2f}%) because at least one of the two person-count fields is NULL. {partial_coverage_text()}"
+    },
+    {
+        "id": 3,
+        "metric": "Recorded deaths per crash",
+        "denominator": "Crash records with both person-injured and person-killed counts non-NULL",
+        "grouping": "Day 6 a.m.–5:59 p.m. versus night 6 p.m.–5:59 a.m.",
+        "chart_type": "Two-bar comparison",
+        "reason": "Deaths per crash isolates the most severe recorded outcome and captures multiple deaths in a single crash.",
+        "probability": 0.25,
+        "answer": f"The file records {rate3_n:.4f} deaths per complete nighttime crash versus {rate3_d:.4f} per complete daytime crash.",
+        "interpretation": f"This framing answers whether nighttime crashes have a higher fatality burden by dividing recorded deaths by crashes with complete person injury and death counts; the chart shows {rate3_n:.4f} deaths per nighttime crash and {rate3_d:.4f} per daytime crash. This is defensible because it counts deaths directly and includes crashes with multiple deaths, but it says nothing about nonfatal injury severity or risk per trip. It leaves out {missing_n} of {total_n} rows ({missing_share:.2f}%) because at least one of the injury or death count fields is NULL. {partial_coverage_text()}"
+    }
+]}
+(OUT / "options.json").write_text(json.dumps(options, indent=2) + "\n")
+print("Coverage:", dict(coverage))
+print("Values 1:\n", volume.to_string(index=False))
+print("Values 2:\n", severity.to_string(index=False))
+print("Values 3:\n", fatality.to_string(index=False))
+print("Saved outputs to", OUT)
*** End Patch
